characterization_methods.key_findings: The polycrystalline as-cast alloys (Al 4-18 at.%, including nominal 7 at.% Al) showed a coarse grain structure with grain sizes of the order of 1 mm; the as-cast alloys contained no second phases.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: specimens etched with an alcoholic 10% nitric acid solution
characterization_methods.purpose: reveal grain boundaries and precipitates, and inspect the coarse grain structure and absence of second phases

characterization_methods.key_findings: For the nominal Fe-7%Al alloy the real (measured) Al content and the C content were not determined (n.d.), as listed in Table 1.
SEM/EDX was applied to fracture surfaces and precipitate analysis of the alloys; no carbides or second phases were found in the as-cast condition.
characterization_methods.purpose: study of fracture surfaces and qualitative precipitate analysis
characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray diffraction (EDX)

interfaces.interface_notes: In the as-cast condition the polycrystalline alloy contained no second phases and the grain boundaries were free of the fine thin platelike or rod-like (carbide) precipitates that appear only after slow furnace cooling from 1100 °C or prolonged heat treatments (e.g. 14 days at 320 °C).

processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles followed by solidification in Cu moulds
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Binary Fe-Al alloy with nominal 7 at.% Al; prepared from Fe of 99.99% purity (purified by zone melting to minimise impurity content) and Al of 99.999% purity; cast into rods usually 18 mm in diameter. The alloy is used in the as-cast condition, i.e. without any subsequent heat treatment (real Al and C contents of the nominal Fe-7%Al alloy were not determined, Table 1).

processing_steps.method: specimens cut by electrostatic discharge machining, mechanically polished and cleansed by ultrasound in acetone
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: No heat treatment was applied to the as-cast sample; heat treatments described in the paper (up to 600 °C, 1100 °C etc.) pertain to other sample conditions, not to this as-cast sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Yield stress determined as 0.2% proof stress in compression (total straining of at least 5%); usually two specimens of each alloy tested, data differing by 3% at most; specimens ground and (for monocrystals) polished with 3 µm diamond paste before testing.

yield_strength.value: linear increase of yield stress with Al content of 21 MPa per at.% Al at 10^-2 s^-1 (higher rate) and 23 MPa per at.% Al at 10^-4 s^-1 (lower rate) at room temperature

structures.overall_structure: Polycrystalline as-cast alloy with a coarse grain structure; the as-cast alloys contained no second phases.

unmapped_findings: Fe-7%Al nominal composition: the real Al content and the C (carbon) content were not determined (n.d.) in Table 1, so the actual composition and impurity level of this specific alloy are unreported. [b0025]

The polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys with Al contents 4-18 at.% (the series that includes the nominal 7 at.% Al alloy) all had coarse grain structures of the order of 1 mm and contained no second phases in the as-cast condition. [b0022]

The observed room-temperature yield-stress increase with Al content corresponds to a solid-solution hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa for polycrystalline alloys with 0-18% Al (not sensitive to deformation rate or temperature), which is described by Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys; this contrasts with ~1 GPa reported for monocrystals. [b0058]

For the as-cast polycrystalline alloys, the ductility (elongation before necking and fracture strain) decreases with increasing Al content: ductile fracture for Al contents up to about 15 at.% Al at room temperature and up to about 12 at.% Al at -100 °C, with a transition to brittle fracture without necking in the range 15-18 at.% Al at room temperature and 12-14 at.% Al at -100 °C. The nominal 7 at.% Al alloy lies in the ductile regime. [b0059, b0070]
At -100 °C the tensile yield stress and ultimate tensile strength of the as-cast polycrystalline alloys are higher than at room temperature by about 80 MPa. [b0038]

The tensile yield stress of the as-cast polycrystalline alloys equals that measured in compression at the same rate and temperature, and the ultimate tensile strength parallels the yield stress. [b0038]
